builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: ADAPT: Agentic Diff-Aware Patch Testing for Pull Requests
summary: This method replaces traditional test generation techniques that optimize for broad code coverage rather than the specific behavior introduced in a pull request. It costs the inference fees of an API-based coding agent and the CI compute required to iteratively execute candidate tests against both the base and head versions. Adoption can fail if the repository lacks the necessary isolated execution environments to safely and automatically run agent-generated code, or if the agent's API costs exceed the allocated budget.
rationale: The technique is highly practical for constrained teams as it relies entirely on accessible third-party APIs and standard CI compute to immediately improve regression testing coverage.

claims.statement: This method replaces traditional test generation techniques that optimize for broad code coverage rather than the specific behavior introduced in a pull request. It costs the inference fees of an API-based coding agent and the CI compute required to iteratively execute candidate tests against both the base and head versions. Adoption can fail if the repository lacks the necessary isolated execution environments to safely and automatically run agent-generated code, or if the agent's API costs exceed the allocated budget.
ADAPT achieves an 89.9% fail-to-pass rate (383/426 PRs) using GPT-5-mini, significantly outperforming the prior state-of-the-art baseline's 35.4% (151/426).
